name: Missouri

agency.name: Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations, Division of Workers' Compensation

ttd.rateText: Sixty-six and two-thirds percent of the injured employee's average weekly earnings, not more than 105% of the state average weekly wage and never less than $40 per week (RSMo 287.170.1(4)-(5)).
ttd.minText: Statutory floor of $40 per week for injuries on or after September 28, 1981 (RSMo 287.170.1(5)).
ttd.periodLabel: injuries on or after July 1, 2026 (fiscal year July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027)

waiting.text: No compensation for the first three days or less of disability during which the employer is open for business, unless the disability lasts longer than fourteen days; then the first three days are paid retroactively (RSMo 287.160.1).

ttdDuration.text: TTD is paid for not more than 400 weeks during the continuance of the disability (RSMo 287.170.1).

ppd.text: PPD is paid in addition to TTD for a number of weeks from the statutory schedule of losses (e.g. arm at shoulder 232 weeks, hand at wrist 175 weeks, thumb 60 weeks) or as a percentage of 400 weeks for body-as-a-whole injuries (RSMo 287.190); the weekly PPD maximum is $678.18 for injuries on or after July 1, 2026. Complete loss of a member increases the scheduled weeks by 10% (DWC chart WC-110).

facts.text: Missouri's FY2027 state average weekly wage is $1,233.06; a weekly wage of $1,942.07 is needed to reach the TTD maximum and $1,017.27 to reach the PPD maximum (DWC memo, July 1, 2026).
An employee is disqualified from TTD for any period in which he or she applies for and receives unemployment compensation (RSMo 287.170.3).
If the employee is fired from post-injury employment for post-injury misconduct, neither TTD nor TPD is payable (RSMo 287.170.4).
For 2026 employers pay a 3.0% Second Injury Fund surcharge plus a 1.5% administrative tax and a 1.5% administrative surcharge (DWC notices).
Compensation must be paid as wages were paid before the injury, and at least once every two weeks (RSMo 287.160.2).
